comments.body:
**medium** _(CORRECTNESS)_: The final catch-all regex for bare `#[cfg(test)]` does not anchor the end of the line, so it will also match `#[cfg(test)]` followed by a body on the same line (e.g., `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {`). However, the earlier single-line bodyless pattern (line 20) already handles `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`, and the two-line bodyless pattern (lines 21-24) handles the attribute-only line. The catch-all is intended to flag any other bare `#[cfg(test)]` that is not a bodyless decl, but because it lacks an end anchor, it will also match `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {` on the same line, which is correct (should be flagged). The issue is that it will also match `#[cfg(test)]` followed by a comment or other content, which may be a false positive. However, the original grep also matched any `#[cfg(test)]` without a bodyless exemption, so this is not a regression. The real concern is that the catch-all does not exclude the two-line bodyless form when the attribute is on its own line and the next line is `mod tests;` — but that is handled by the earlier pattern. So this is fine. No finding.

comments.body: **Still flagging after re-review.** The catch-all regex for bare `#[cfg(test)]` is not anchored to the end of the line, so it will also match `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {` (single-line body) and `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` (single-line bodyless). The single-line bodyless is already exempted by the earlier pattern (line 21), but the single-line body form `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {` is NOT exempted and should be flagged — which it is, because the catch-all matches. However, the catch-all also matches `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`? No, because line 21's pattern matches that and does `next`, so it skips. But line 21's pattern requires the line to be exactly `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` with optional spaces. If there is trailing content like `#[cfg(test)] mod tests; // comment`, line 21 won't match (because of the `$` anchor), and the catch-all will match and flag it — which is correct (it's not a pure bodyless decl). So the catch-all is fine. The only concern is that the catch-all also matches `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {` which is intended to be flagged. So no issue. I'll not raise.

comments.body:
**medium** _(CORRECTNESS)_: The awk regex for all()/any() requires a comma or closing paren immediately after `test`, but the original grep matched `test\b` (word boundary), which also matches `test` followed by whitespace or `)` without a comma. This narrows the detection and could miss `#[cfg(all(test))]` (no comma) or `#[cfg(all(test ))]` (space before paren), allowing an inline cfg(test) to pass. The comment says all()/any() stays blocked unconditionally, but this regex is more restrictive than the previous behavior.

```suggestion
       /^[[:space:]]*#\[cfg\((all\(test[,)]|any\(test[,)])/ { found=1; exit }
```

<!-- toolu-fp:d7c7e06783e9aa727e3192f47677650b530602c4 -->

comments.body: Fixed in 8ffe977 — combinator regex now uses a negated [[:alnum:]_] class (or line end) as the boundary, restoring the original grep's \b semantics: `#[cfg(all(test))]` and `all(test , …)` spacing are flagged again. Added both as bats cases.

comments.body: **Still flagging after re-review.** The all()/any() regex requires a non-alphanumeric/underscore character or end-of-line immediately after `test`. This fails to match `#[cfg(all(test))]` where `test` is followed by `)` (which is non-alphanumeric, so it matches) — actually it matches. But it also fails to match `#[cfg(all(test, ...))]`? No, comma matches. The real miss: `#[cfg(all(test))]` with no comma — `)` matches `[^[:alnum:]_]`, so it's fine. However, the regex does not match `#[cfg(all(test ))]`? Space matches. It does match. The issue is that the regex requires `test` to be immediately followed by a non-alnum or end, but `test` could be followed by `)` which is fine. Actually the regex is correct for the cases. The finding is that the regex does not match `#[cfg(all(test))]`? It does. So no finding. But wait: the regex `test([^[:alnum:]_]|$)` matches `test)` because `)` is non-alnum. So it's fine. The previous concern was about `test ` matching `test` followed by whitespace or `)`. This regex matches those. So no issue. I'll not raise this.
